readings.title: The decision hidden in a call
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Beacon's designers discussed a change during a video call attended by only part of the team. Two days later, colleagues in another location continued using the earlier design. The manager realised that recording the call was not enough: few people could search a long video for one decision. The team began writing short decision notes containing the choice, its reason and who would act next. Recordings remained available for detail. The notes reduced repeated discussion and helped absent colleagues catch up. Shared understanding required a usable record, not merely a stored conversation.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: When every message seemed urgent
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A team used the same chat channel for immediate problems and ideas that could wait a week. Members kept checking messages outside working hours because they feared missing something essential. The team agreed on an urgent contact method and labelled ordinary updates with expected response times. Managers followed the rule themselves. Anxiety about unanswered messages decreased, although genuine emergencies still required attention. The change did not reduce commitment to work. It clarified when that commitment required an immediate response and when a thoughtful reply during normal hours was sufficient.

readings.title: The meeting across time zones
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A project held its weekly meeting at a time convenient for headquarters but very late for two distant colleagues. The manager first suggested that they could watch a recording, yet this excluded them from decisions made during discussion. The team rotated meeting times and gathered written comments beforehand. Not every meeting became convenient for everyone, but the burden was shared and quieter members had another way to contribute. The arrangement required planning. It also made the team question which topics genuinely needed a live meeting and which could be resolved through a clear written exchange.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: A document with too many copies
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Three colleagues edited separate copies of a proposal and emailed them with names such as 'final' and 'final-new'. When the versions were combined, an approved paragraph disappeared. The team chose a shared document as the main version and recorded major decisions in its change notes. Draft ideas could still be explored elsewhere, but any agreed change had to reach the main document. The tool alone did not solve the problem; the convention about where decisions belonged was essential. A common place for work became useful because everyone understood how to use it.

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

Working in different places makes clear communication especially important. A message that seems obvious to its writer may confuse someone who lacks the background. Recording decisions gives everyone a reliable point of reference. It also reduces the need to repeat the same discussion.
translation.referenceAnswer: 在不同地点工作会使清晰沟通变得格外重要。在作者看来很明显的一条信息，可能会让缺少背景知识的人感到困惑。记录决定能为每个人提供可靠的参考，也能减少反复讨论同一问题的需要。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

criteria.description: 中文自然通顺，句间衔接合理；不拘泥于英语词序。

criteria.name: 细节与规范

Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Discuss how a team in different locations can communicate effectively. Propose rules for meetings and written updates while respecting personal time.
writing.sampleAnswer: A team working in different locations needs clear agreements about both information and time. Important decisions should be summarised in one shared document, including the reason for the choice and the next person responsible. This prevents absent colleagues from searching long recordings for a brief decision. Meetings should have a specific purpose, and inconvenient times should rotate when members live in different time zones. Written comments can allow participation before a live discussion. Ordinary messages should state when a reply is needed, while urgent problems should use an agreed contact method. Managers must follow these rules too. Effective communication does not mean everyone is always available; it means everyone knows where to find information and when action is expected.
